## Israel Attacks Iran
Israeli officials confirmed last night that their air force [bombed military targets](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0kLFuhDAQRL_GdD7ZC2dw4SIN3aVNiRZYuE0MRmvrTvx9RPp0I83ozWi-HsMDOfK-fuJGoSxpAAONtkaDG2bkeA5NNYeFCKiuKNgWvK99Z0z1DNi1_o4TusWNxtiWRutc203GT7Wtqak4XDRrwFlT-zvcqF46u8zOOztPHkk1hmYuSW7fiffypCWe6UVym9JWxfAs5ciq_lDQK-j380i5XJaC_gIr6K259F1B_04SZ73TOyvoOQtS1AsLZS1UMDKWJKfORfiHNK7Iey6aBXd9FeoRY-RceNIb58yR9IgiuJIWOpIUBX0lYT7efOVcqxqzbsjxb2n577lXgN8AAAD___jocak) near Tehran in response to Iranian missile strikes. 140 Israeli planes [targeted missile production facilities](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0kLFu8yAUhZ8Gb1hwcYgZGH7pl6UO6drRujYX-1YEIpsmSp6-cqcunc_ROZ--j8t4QU6cl3e8kq-xjKCgk1pJsGNATs-xa4KPRECmIa_P4JxxvVLN6pFwgqCnGCfnOmtjQINzdLYnheEEDftjTSuwWhl3gpZM7HUM1lkdZockOkWBa9naz8K5rhTTs9xpa-dybZJfa73twvwTMAgYcJozPfZ2KUcsYHjLlbaMlUvGJGBIfCf5dQtYaRcw8L4hJbngC2WiCXPJ8ndFcoiy4rZQ5bzIlV5TSQnX480MHIT5r3XnemX6U7P5cHtwSrzbs-jUckVOP5T1L2t3D98BAAD__0wpcO4) near Tehran, along with Iranian air defense systems, drones, and ballistic missile transmitters. "_We’re targeting things that might have threatened us in the past or could do in the future_ ," an Israeli spokesman said. An Israeli news outlet has also claimed that the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps was hit by the air strikes. U.S. officials said [they were notified](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0z7GO8yAQBOCnwZ0tWGwwBcXfuMvfXmltYEn2jpgIo_jy9idff91II32j-bisF-TM2-0_Psi3VFaQMPZK9mDWiJzf69hFn4iAdEdeWXBOu1nK7u4DOTcpdw02RWuCivZKagI9G6nmyULH_tSUBKOkdhMMpNOsUjTOqBgckhglRW6lDp-Ft3anlN_lRXUI5dFlf2_tuQv9T8AiYDmOY8BvLvvZClhOW8Ci5JknAQvvFSn32BqGr73niltfqWFmbFy2rvr4PDhn3o0Vo7w9kPPvUvvr-cvDTwAAAP__qjBZeQ) hours before the attack and that no U.S. forces were involved.
## Virginia Ordered to Restore Noncitizen Voters
A federal judge ruled Friday that Virginia improperly [purged 1,600 noncitizen voters](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0kL1ugzAUhZ_GbBf5L4AHD13Y0rUjcvA1ODVcZBxQ3r5K1XbreHQ-fTo6H9fh6mKK6_TuFrQl0CC51CA4yGbwLqbnoCtvA6JEVaEVrTRGmY7zarZBKd9cOhQ33-lRC2xl212w5QJNG7iuon3ZBJeN4MpcZI0qdCL4xjTCj8Yh0xx9LJTrO8W1zBjSkw7M9UhLlexcyrYz9cZkz2R_nmd95ji-Sib7Fc-dyf6IeYprdPCTA3rMLsH94ScEyh7zDn9QIZhdKnBQwQwZFzpcgi3TlN0C26PAhrQlhJsbP4HWX5BSesmrbP12xpTi3rRM82lxMX2PLf-dd1j5FQAA__-1wHTT) from its rolls too close to Election Day, granting an injunction requested by the Justice Department. Virginia passed a law in 2006 that allows the state to use DMV data to remove voters unable to verify their citizenship—a law approved of by the DOJ and used by both parties since. On Oct. 11th, however, the [Justice Department filed a suit](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0kLuO5CAQRb8GZ1jlwo8mINjE2Wy6oUVDYdeIhhYwtma_fuXNJ7-Po_PnY_uwHDntv-2LTAt5Q8BRDiBx3rzl-L2NnTeBCEl1ZIYFtVb6AdAdxgON4B40uaeeYFlIB3DPSQH4CZfZdmzutQFwHkDpCXtS4TEEP-t58E5bEiOQ55ZL_5k5tYNC_M4nld7lVxfN0dq7CvVL4Cpwva6rT0932Xpw2ltOd0rg6slx5ZzkfSZw_fzyO8lcPJUqTy47J7ayZVmotlxIDjOAPHOjIgvtXFuxjXOq0tnkKJKXnCSFkEu7a--vspNMOTlu_JdSFbiqZYIFlcC1K8a_L46R67yIEfaX5fifv_3k8zT4LwAA__98rXnt) that claimed Virginia was violating a provision of the National Voter Registration Act by removing names within 90 days of an election. Virginia Gov. Glenn Youngkin announced [plans to file an emergency appeal](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx00DFuwyAUgOHT4A0Lnh1sBoYu3tK1o0XCg5BgQJgY-fZVO3TrBX59-r-u61X74KP71BuqatMKDEbKGQWxGu3DuY6dURYRcOhQ8QmkHOTMWPdQcpqZ4JMFCbPUYgSO8w0FH6S0N2uw8-qnxhkIzgZ5gR4HO3NrhBTc3KVGMjI0vqbSP5OP9YE2nOnA0t_T1gX1qDXvZPggsBBYWmt9O6rtU3EElohtJ7D8eS8EFosGiw70-TYO6S2k-2unR6pYaH4XhzSX5Ire6Jne0b18pEdqO9WR6pxRh64ok5sPwe9iIiNzm_bhF1P_m3Mo-A4AAP__d7ZnOQ) with the Fourth Circuit Court to block the ruling, stating his administration would take the case to the U.S. Supreme Court if needed.
## List: Most Halloween Obsessed States
New England is the most festive region for Halloween, with New Hampshire and Maine ranked as [the top "Halloween-obsessed"](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx00L2OwyAQBOCngY4I1r8UFNe4y7VXWsjsBi4YUCCx8vYnp7_608xI83NdrzbEkG7fdkfTKK8goRdKChhXZ0N8rz13hhABO45GTaB1p2cpuTfDhpPTk5tnSW5DGqhXhIPVRDQ5mHgwZ5uSMCrZ6QEu2NGsyI16VG7TFlkv0YWWH5ffHFLzSPGdX_i4bHnn0fjWSmXdF4OFwdI8-hDjaQwWn3dMeFQGS222oThs2zyDpddDN8-j8DbGfCAm8fEqasn5_hYVbc1JlOde7iGJcsaEt8_U0AmfnxUZLPxhXDlCjKGOE-vlbbfhs8zbfy-9DPwFAAD__y6LbJY) states in the country, according to a new ranking. ConsumerAffairs analyzed data on haunted attractions, pumpkin patches, and Spirit Halloween stores relative to each state's population, along with internet search data. New Hampshire and Maine were joined by Utah, Idaho, and West Virginia in the top five. The top five least festive areas in the nation were Washington, D.C., New York, Florida, Georgia, and Hawaii. body:
Hi, Peter. It's James Carville and Paul Begala.
We know a thing or two about close elections, so take our word when we say we’re _extremely concerned about what we’re seeing in Pennsylvania’s Senate race._
If you don’t believe us, we prepared a brief memo highlighting the key factors of this race for you.
[**If you don’t need convincing, rush a donation to Bob Casey’s campaign now.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20241026-1?refcode=em20241026-1&refcode2=4680_552475_V0ppAS&akid=4680%2E552475%2EV0ppAS)
**[Donate ››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20241026-1?refcode=em20241026-1&refcode2=4680_552475_V0ppAS&akid=4680%2E552475%2EV0ppAS)**
**OCTOBER CAMPAIGN MEMO ON PA-SEN** **FROM:** James Carville and Paul Begala, Senior Democratic Strategists
**TO:** Interested Parties We need to be clear with you about where things stand in this battleground Senate race. **The Senate race in Pennsylvania is in a dead heat.**
* A number of polling agencies and political experts have released figures showing that Bob Casey’s race will be one of the closest on the map.
* Trafalgar Poll: David McCormick 47.2% – Bob Casey 46.8%
* Washington Post Poll: Bob Casey 48% – David McCormick 48%
* CNN Poll: Bob Casey 46% – David McCormick 46%
* RealClearPolitics: PA Senate race is a tossup.
* Cook Political Report: PA Senate Race is a Toss Up
* The numbers tell some clear signs. This is one of the closest Senate races in the country.

**McCormick and GOP billionaires are spending more than $150 million to flip this battleground.**
* With 10 days left until Election Day, this campaign is being outspent by tens of millions and is at risk of being drowned out on the airwaves.
* Keystone Renewal, one of the largest single-candidate super PACs in history, is spending more than $56 million supporting David McCormick. That’s unheard of in Senate races this cycle.
* The Senate Leadership Fund, a Mitch McConnell-linked super PAC, is spending $24 million to defeat Bob Casey.
* David McCormick has continued to self-fund his campaign with millions from his personal fortune, and you can expect more opposition ad spending in the final weeks.
* While Pennsylvanians are being inundated with GOP attack ads, Bob Casey’s campaign might have to go dark if they don’t have the resources to keep up. In a race this close, that could be the difference between winning and losing.

**Pennsylvania has historically been the tipping point for U.S. Elections.**
* We’ve been on both the winning and losing side of elections, and here’s what we know for sure: _As PA goes, so goes the nation._
* In 2016, 44,292 votes in PA propelled Donald Trump to his unexpected win.
* In 2020, Joe Biden clinched Pennsylvania’s 20 electoral votes by a narrow 1.17% margin, helping him secure the White House.
* Nate Silver’s model is predicting that whichever presidential candidate wins PA has over a 93% chance of winning.
* When charting a path to a Democratic Senate majority, **_Pennsylvania is a must-win race._**

**Bob Casey needs the resources to make his case.**
* In order to win, this campaign needs to make the case directly to voters about the threat David McCormick poses to Pennsylvanians' fundamental freedoms -- and that takes organizing and advertising.

---
Listen, Peter, after crunching the numbers, one thing is clear: Bob Casey needs your help.
[**So please, if you want to make sure Democrats win the Senate and White House this year, donate $5 or more to Bob’s re-election campaign right now. This may be the most important moment of this cycle.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20241026-1?refcode=em20241026-1&refcode2=4680_552475_V0ppAS&akid=4680%2E552475%2EV0ppAS)
**[Donate $5 ››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20241026-1?refcode=em20241026-1&refcode2=4680_552475_V0ppAS&akid=4680%2E552475%2EV0ppAS)**
Thank you for your support.
— James Carville and Paul Begala

clean_body: Hi, Peter. It's James Carville and Paul Begala. We know a thing or two about close elections, so take our word when we say we’re extremely concerned about what we’re seeing in Pennsylvania’s Senate race. If you don’t believe us, we prepared a brief memo highlighting the key factors of this race for you. OCTOBER CAMPAIGN MEMO ON PA-SEN FROM: James Carville and Paul Begala, Senior Democratic Strategists TO: Interested Parties We need to be clear with you about where things stand in this battleground Senate race. The Senate race in Pennsylvania is in a dead heat. A number of polling agencies and political experts have released figures showing that Bob Casey’s race will be one of the closest on the map. Trafalgar Poll: David McCormick 47.2% – Bob Casey 46.8% Washington Post Poll: Bob Casey 48% – David McCormick 48% CNN Poll: Bob Casey 46% – David McCormick 46% RealClearPolitics: PA Senate race is a tossup. Cook Political Report: PA Senate Race is a Toss Up The numbers tell some clear signs. This is one of the closest Senate races in the country. McCormick and GOP billionaires are spending more than $150 million to flip this battleground. With 10 days left until Election Day, this campaign is being outspent by tens of millions and is at risk of being drowned out on the airwaves. Keystone Renewal, one of the largest single-candidate super PACs in history, is spending more than $56 million supporting David McCormick. That’s unheard of in Senate races this cycle. The Senate Leadership Fund, a Mitch McConnell-linked super PAC, is spending $24 million to defeat Bob Casey. David McCormick has continued to self-fund his campaign with millions from his personal fortune, and you can expect more opposition ad spending in the final weeks. While Pennsylvanians are being inundated with GOP attack ads, Bob Casey’s campaign might have to go dark if they don’t have the resources to keep up. In a race this close, that could be the difference between winning and losing. Pennsylvania has historically been the tipping point for U.S. Elections. We’ve been on both the winning and losing side of elections, and here’s what we know for sure: As PA goes, so goes the nation. In 2016, 44,292 votes in PA propelled Donald Trump to his unexpected win. In 2020, Joe Biden clinched Pennsylvania’s 20 electoral votes by a narrow 1.17% margin, helping him secure the White House. Nate Silver’s model is predicting that whichever presidential candidate wins PA has over a 93% chance of winning. When charting a path to a Democratic Senate majority, Pennsylvania is a must-win race. Bob Casey needs the resources to make his case. In order to win, this campaign needs to make the case directly to voters about the threat David McCormick poses to Pennsylvanians' fundamental freedoms -- and that takes organizing and advertising. Listen, Peter, after crunching the numbers, one thing is clear: Bob Casey needs your help. Thank you for your support. — James Carville and Paul Begala

My mom taught me that if I wanted to succeed, I had to roll up my sleeves and get the job done. And you know what? We got the job done. I'll roll up my sleeves, work tirelessly, and get the job done. No excuses, no delays, no more broken promises. But I need your help to get there. subject: My decision

body:
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2127%2E135344%2EQkblTB)

[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-oct24.UCjdR-&refcode=em241026-1-900&t=2&akid=2127%2E135344%2EQkblTB)
---
Friends --
While I know our campaign has sent a lot of emails ahead of Election Day, I want to take a few minutes to tell you about my decision to run for Senate in the first place, and why your support is so important in our success.
The truth is, we all know America is _going through something_ right now. We seem to be living from crisis to crisis. But there are certain things that should be really simple:
Like living a middle-class life in the state that invented the middle class.
Like making things in America so that we’re in control of our own economic security.
Like protecting our children from the things that are _truly_ harming them.
And preserving our rights and our democracy so that our kids can live their version of the American dream.
**I’m running for Senate because I believe that we need a new generation of leaders that thinks differently, works harder, and never forgets the mission of public service.**
But my decision to run for Senate is also deeply personal to me, and it's related to what motivated me to first run for the House in 2018.
It's about my mom, Judy. She was diagnosed with stage IV ovarian cancer in 2009 — and didn't have health insurance at the time. She had let it lapse after the insurance companies had gouged her for years because she happened to have a pre-existing condition. She passed away in 2011, but that experience — of desperately trying to get her care at the same moment we were filling out bankruptcy paperwork — fueled me to run. I remember the exact moment that made me run: when the then-GOP controlled House of Representatives, the body I now serve in, voted to repeal those protections for people with pre-existing conditions.
Seven years later, the Republican leaders, fueled by the extreme wing of the party, are continuing the march to repeal things that the average Americans want. They want to privatize Social Security and Medicare, repeal drug price protections like allowing Medicare to negotiate, then there’s the rights they’re obsessed with repealing: a woman’s right to choose, voting rights, and any possible gun safety legislation.
By winning this Senate seat, we’ll help ensure that Democrats retain the (slight!) majority and can pass legislation that expands access to healthcare. Not the obsession with taking things away.
To be upfront: **Winning this race is going to take a lot of resources. A crazy amount. And we have to do it without raising a single dollar from corporate PACs.**
[**That is why I would love it if you would consider donating $3 or whatever you can to my campaign as we're now in the final sprint.](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-oct24.UCjdR-&refcode=em241026-1-900&t=3&akid=2127%2E135344%2EQkblTB)**

Biz here with a confession — I never fully recovered from Obama 2008. That election turned me into an organizer, and these final days before an election brings out the nitty-gritty organizer in me. Here’s what I’m focused on: **Right now, in many races up and down the ballot, the margins look slim.** If recent elections are any indication, these small margins will have huge implications:
* The 2020 presidential election was decided by fewer than 100,000 votes across three states.
* In 2022, one Democracy Defender in Minnesota won her race by just 321 votes. That win helped flip control of the Minnesota State Senate to the Democrats.

**Peter, it’s time to focus everything on turning out Democrats to vote.** Those margins from past years show that every get–out–the–vote (GOTV) conversation we have in the next 10 days can help decide the outcome in the most important races for our democracy across the country. [**It’s time to GOTV. LFG, Peter. Help fight for Democracy Defenders with everything we can do in the next 10 days — and beyond. It was a tangible problem that I wanted to fix. That’s why I do this work, and I know that Democrats like you support the NDRC’s multi-pronged approach to address this root issue facing our democracy.
**The NDRC uses every possible tool to create a more representative democracy.** Right now we’re focused on supporting Democracy Defenders in the most impactful races across the country. In 2022, one Democracy Defender in Minnesota won her race by just 321 votes. That win helped flip control of the Minnesota State Senate to the Democrats. Peter, it’s time to focus everything on turning out Democrats to vote. Dear dpwillis67@gmail.com, You may ask, “Why would you want a holster that fits under your arm?” Because when out and about, concealed carry is the most [responsible form of self defense.](https://links.nationalgunowner.org/a/1537/click/18910/6374453/4cdf8edf1052b91d1fe9614cf48319b165994f4c/7e6d81054a691f05f3570f0e0b1b370e2d375d84) I am not one for brandishing any weapon. In fact, my goal is to have it remain so discreet, no one will EVER know I am carrying. That’s TRUE self-defense. You know it’s there... But you never have to use it. [So I keep mine close by, tucked away.](https://links.nationalgunowner.org/a/1537/click/18910/6374453/4cdf8edf1052b91d1fe9614cf48319b165994f4c/7e6d81054a691f05f3570f0e0b1b370e2d375d84)

It’s easy to retrieve when I put it in my safe at night. And it’s secure, so it will stay exactly where I want it. You might be thinking about getting one, And in my humble opinion, **[You DEFINITELY should!](https://links.nationalgunowner.org/a/1537/click/18910/6374453/4cdf8edf1052b91d1fe9614cf48319b165994f4c/7e6d81054a691f05f3570f0e0b1b370e2d375d84)**

name: Elissa Slotkin
subject: A difficult decision
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Lucas Kunce for Missouri
body:
Peter —
We made a very difficult decision last week.
We had a Team Slotkin meeting where it became clear that if we had a bit more money, we could make a real play for additional votes as voting was underway across the state.
The money wasn’t in the budget. But I gave the green light.
It’s a risk. But this is the moment to take some risks. I’ve had similar moments in prior years. We can’t get caught short when people are already casting their ballots in this election. That'd be a mistake.
But the bet we made was that, as the race tightens, and if we asked, our supporters would come through to help fill the gap. We hope that you will. To keep the Senate in the hands of the Democrats.
So with that in mind: **[can you make a $10 contribution to Lucas Kunce and my campaign to help us fill the budget gap we created going after the voters we need to persuade to help win this race?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/80596?refcode=em20241026-8232&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=8232%2E614464%2Ecc_par)** $10 isn’t much, but at this point it’s the small-dollar donations that are making a difference here at the end.
Like I said, it was a tough call. But if there’s one thing that distinguishes this campaign from every other, it’s our people. You answer the call every single time. $10 is all we need to close the gap.

name: Douglas Carswell
subject: Politics without a Legacy is Pointless
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/msla-11573303?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| Dear Friend, **“All political lives end in failure” observed the British Prime Minister, Harold Macmillan. **His did. So, too, will Joe Biden’s.

Forced out after four years, it is difficult to think of a single significant achievement by the Biden administration. **Biden’s legacy will be higher national debt and a more divided America.**

But is it really the case that political lives always end in failure?

Watching the recent movie about Ronald Reagan, it was obvious that after two terms in office, the Gipper’s accomplishments clearly outweighed any defeats. **Reagan’s legacy was a buoyant economy, stronger America and the defeat of Soviet communism.**
---
|
---
_Legacy? Good, Bad or Irrelevant ...._
| **If Biden’s legacy is of extreme failure, and Reagan’s of remarkable success, many politicians don’t seem to leave much of a legacy at all, good or bad.** Like footprints on a beach at low tide, tomorrow it will be as though they were never there at all.

**Many politicians fail to leave much of a legacy for the simple reason that they hold office, but have little idea what to do with it.**

That’s not, of course, what they tell themselves in the early days. **In the afterglow of their election victory, surrounded by staffers, and praised by smooth-tongued lobbyists, political leaders busy themselves with the business of government. **

Yet often the urgent squeezes out the important. Once in office, they end up playing the role of Senator, Congressman, or state Governor, like an actor in a movie handed their lines by someone else.

**Rather than implementing a blueprint that matters, they are distracted by the trivial.** Instead of delivering difficult messages, they delude themselves that another press conference about blah blah really matters.

Rare is the type of politician who can make the political weather, rather than respond to it.

**Many politicians fail to leave a legacy because they fool themselves that they are responsible for things that would have happened anyhow. **

Or they imagine that they will be fondly remembered for things that happened on their watch. **How many Mississippians remember who was governor when the Nissan factory came to Mississippi?** How many credit whoever happened to be in office?
---
|
---
_Robert Redford in movie, “The Candidate”; What do we do now?_
| **Any politician in our state wanting to leave a real legacy needs to address those things that have kept our state 50 th out of 50 for too long.**

**First is education.** Mississippi needs a wholesale reform of education, with school choice and parent power. With so many surrounding states implementing universal school choice, change is possible. **The first wave of Mississippi leaders to actually come out and lead on this will be seen to deliver historic changes for the better. **

**Second is the state economy.** Mississippi’s economy continues to be weighed down by a relatively high tax burden and red tape. Despite cutting the state income tax, Mississippi families and business still pay more than in surrounding states. Certificate of Need laws hold back the healthcare economy in our state. **State leaders that lead on lower taxes and deregulation would stand out nationally and historically, like the folks below.**
---
|
---
_State leaders leading_
| These are the issues that will define the future of our state. Our state leaders will be defined by if and how they address them.

**State leaders that address these issues will leave a giant legacy. Those that don’t, won't be a household name in their own home.**

Have a wonderful weekend!
---

My mom didn’t end up winning, but she _never_ backed down, and neither will I.

I’m running for Congress to pick up where my mom and the trailblazers before us left off so we can build a government that truly reflects the great diversity and strength of our nation. clean_body: I’m running for Congress to pick up where my mom and the trailblazers before us left off so we can build a government that truly reflects the great diversity and strength of our nation. | = Peter, In 1988, my mom, Betty Tamposi, ran for this very same Congressional seat after serving our community in the New Hampshire legislature for 6 years. During that race, her opponent’s campaign used the phrase: “A woman’s place is in the home, not in the House.” My mom didn’t end up winning, but she never backed down, and neither will I. Today, women make up less than one-third of the members of Congress, but more and more women across the country are stepping up and running for office than ever before! I’m running for Congress to pick up where my mom and the trailblazers before us left off so we can build a government that truly reflects the great diversity and strength of our nation. That means fighting to defend reproductive freedom, protect our sacred right to vote, and lower costs for hard-working families. It’s time for a new generation of women to flip the script and prove that a woman’s place is in the People’s House – but I can’t do that without your continued support. = | = | = | = | = | = With gratitude, Maggie Goodlander * | | = Paid for by Maggie for Congress Maggie for Congress 131 Daniel Webster Hwy #949 Nashua, NH 03060 United States | | | ---|---|--- = =

| | Dear Friend,

I'm thrilled to introduce an extraordinary opportunity for you...

Perhaps you've wondered where the artwork accompanying the lectures in our free online courses comes from. We hear this especially for one of our most popular courses, "The Genesis Story."

Derek —

* **TOP NEWS**

"**Texas turnout rate slightly down after first three days of early voting,** " San Texas Tribune's **Juan Salinas II** -- "Turnout among Texas voters is slightly down this fall compared to the record-setting 2020 presidential election, according to a Texas Tribune analysis of state data.

More than 2.8 million Texans this year have either voted in person during the first three days of early voting or have returned their ballot by mail. That's 15.1% of all registered voters. In 2020, 15.7% of registered voters went to the polls or turned in their ballot during the same period in 2020.

Texas has more registered voters than ever: 18.6 million, an increase of about 1.7 million since 2020. Voter turnout during that election ended at about 67% -- a modern-day record for the Lone Star State, known for low voter participation.

[Early voting began Monday](https://substack.com/redirect/28ebbf16-3075-4262-b926-b43d96617fac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The last day to vote early is Nov. 1. Texans must return their absentee ballot to their county in person or have their ballot postmarked by Nov. 5, Election Day.

There are caveats to early vote data. It can be incomplete -- each county self-reports to the state. And Texas is offering two weeks of early voting in 2024 compared to an extended three weeks in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. There was also a greater emphasis on mail-in ballots four years ago.

Just two of the state's most populous counties -- Denton and Fort Bend -- have broken their turnout records during the first three days of early voting, the Tribune found. Meanwhile, Dallas, El Paso and Harris counties have seen a drop.

That should be a warning sign for the Texas Democrats, said **Matthew Wilson** , a political science professor at Southern Methodist University.

"If I were a Democratic adviser, that would give me some concern," Wilson said.

Another warning sign for Democrats, who have long hoped to gain a foothold in a state dominated by Republicans, is the voting history of early voters.

More Republicans than Democrats appear to be voting early based on their voting history, said **Derek Ryan** , a veteran consultant and adviser to GOP campaigns. According to his tracking, 1.1 million voters who cast their ballot during the first three days of early voting have previously voted in a Republican primary. That compared to 715,180 voters who participated in a Democratic primary.

At this point in 2020, Republicans and Democrats made up about the same percentage of early vote, according to Ryan's analysis. Meanwhile, in both 2020 and 2024, about a quarter of the early vote was cast by people with no history of voting in a partisan primary election in Texas." ($5/mo or $50/yr or $199 lifetime) TOP NEWS "Texas turnout rate slightly down after first three days of early voting, " San Texas Tribune's Juan Salinas II -- "Turnout among Texas voters is slightly down this fall compared to the record-setting 2020 presidential election, according to a Texas Tribune analysis of state data. More than 2.8 million Texans this year have either voted in person during the first three days of early voting or have returned their ballot by mail. That's 15.1% of all registered voters. In 2020, 15.7% of registered voters went to the polls or turned in their ballot during the same period in 2020. Texas has more registered voters than ever: 18.6 million, an increase of about 1.7 million since 2020. Voter turnout during that election ended at about 67% -- a modern-day record for the Lone Star State, known for low voter participation. . The last day to vote early is Nov. 1. Texans must return their absentee ballot to their county in person or have their ballot postmarked by Nov. 5, Election Day. There are caveats to early vote data. It can be incomplete -- each county self-reports to the state. And Texas is offering two weeks of early voting in 2024 compared to an extended three weeks in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. There was also a greater emphasis on mail-in ballots four years ago. Just two of the state's most populous counties -- Denton and Fort Bend -- have broken their turnout records during the first three days of early voting, the Tribune found. Meanwhile, Dallas, El Paso and Harris counties have seen a drop. That should be a warning sign for the Texas Democrats, said Matthew Wilson , a political science professor at Southern Methodist University. "If I were a Democratic adviser, that would give me some concern," Wilson said. Another warning sign for Democrats, who have long hoped to gain a foothold in a state dominated by Republicans, is the voting history of early voters. More Republicans than Democrats appear to be voting early based on their voting history, said Derek Ryan , a veteran consultant and adviser to GOP campaigns. According to his tracking, 1.1 million voters who cast their ballot during the first three days of early voting have previously voted in a Republican primary. That compared to 715,180 voters who participated in a Democratic primary. At this point in 2020, Republicans and Democrats made up about the same percentage of early vote, according to Ryan's analysis. Meanwhile, in both 2020 and 2024, about a quarter of the early vote was cast by people with no history of voting in a partisan primary election in Texas." Why are you hearing from me?

**Well, I was raised in New Jersey. I love this state._And I love this country._**

I have been a known conservative in Hollywood throughout my career. It wasn’t always easy, but the latest from the bankrupt elites in my town really got to me.

After President Trump was shot, the only echo reverberating through my so-called “community” was a regret that the assassin failed to kill him. Weeks later, on a zoom call: White Dudes for Kamala. In a masterpiece of intolerance, in a breathtakingly short period of time, we learned what they are all about: _Hatred and Racism._ **Pathetic**.

I refuse to rail about the Democrats and what they have inflicted upon this country. We all know about their shortcomings, and we all know the kind of future we can bank on should they remain in power.

[**I believe Curtis Bashaw is the right kind of man to send to Washington to promote well-being in New Jersey and the United States at large. We can look to him to protect the Jersey Shore.**](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=551041b04df845e5bc868f7a9b223b32&_e=CQ7PogR2tIatzJShWaNPNq2nPAuEGtne6BrJc749gG1L5k8heEpqPd5rlehG1-97HMjaPvhL9Fbxjhg2sYsOpVhxE1dxfh7CGMhJPc76KOmp5LlJRqXmkzgLc6_RkSHkTeOTTh1QgybjcK12Mh6nkNJnXUo9zPVIt4l4S_OmxrCZhgpS8cOMBNwJRrFDrjhvWYujttSbAvTAf6dSse33iuRXdvYaqffn6x8PfGLIT5DKghavDiPoWPeNBotSgNNNYctWiOBVlQYUF1dCCEiObonIFh5QemPWwZh0ygWGm8cKdekS_nXceTHXJ7ibTMgM-1szuXNvJ7NNwJNXqO8QFp05QLLt5B_0dB2JWWyiuo5YU4kqiKiCOyjjW-6J2RMJPY_Qvmrfb5gLjdWE0w1-aOXWFl44RqkIft8Gfy_fNis%3D)

We can look to him to promote prosperity for all—a good paycheck and food we can afford. But more importantly, he is a good man. A man of good character. A man whose voice can be trusted as he raises his hand to preserve the Constitution of the United States. Our Constitution.

[**There comes a time when we have to speak out in support of our nation’s traditional values. For Patriotism. For the right to pursue happiness on our own terms.**](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=551041b04df845e5bc868f7a9b223b32&_e=CQ7PogR2tIatzJShWaNPNq2nPAuEGtne6BrJc749gG1L5k8heEpqPd5rlehG1-97HMjaPvhL9Fbxjhg2sYsOpVhxE1dxfh7CGMhJPc76KOmp5LlJRqXmkzgLc6_RkSHkTeOTTh1QgybjcK12Mh6nkNJnXUo9zPVIt4l4S_OmxrCZhgpS8cOMBNwJRrFDrjhvWYujttSbAvTAf6dSse33iuRXdvYaqffn6x8PfGLIT5DKghavDiPoWPeNBotSgNNNYctWiOBVlQYUF1dCCEiObi0ZPLGH5Ln1fB9i121F3c4LoZBr4jDxJ29fJDNUcMfGviSnTw5saKi9XCSbt0-OvYOfy9ivtQNLiRDjQV7c4IIbbN2NMwHZ2lxdij7gNBxDsaZkm91gnkHLH38U1P0tstWsRqrgOjGKjF2Z4yJascs%3D)

We need a remedy for what Washington has been doing.

Curtis Bashaw in the United States Senate could be that remedy or at least a good part of it.

Please join me in supporting Curtis Bashaw.

Cheerfully and flag-wavingly yours!

Kelsey Grammer

| **_GET TO KNOW CURTIS_**

**Curtis Bashaw is a hotel entrepreneur, job creator, and preservationist. He's running for United States Senate to provide greater freedom and opportunities for all New Jerseyans.**

A lifelong New Jersey resident, Curtis grew up in Camden County and spent his summers at the Jersey Shore working as a bellhop and waiting tables at Congress Hall in Cape May. He has spent his life in the real estate and hospitality industries, and is the Founder and Managing Partner of Cape Resorts, a hotel company focusing on the restoration and operation of classic American resort properties in New Jersey and New York.

Throughout his career, Curtis has worked to build communities and bring people together. He is widely recognized for leading the landmark restorations of Congress Hall and the Virginia Hotel in Cape May, and for launching creative programming to dramatically extend Cape May's season, a catalyst for the economic rebirth of one of the Jersey Shore's most beautiful communities.

Curtis is a successful businessman and job creator, employing more than 1,000 people in New Jersey and New York. Curtis' company owns and operates eight hotels, ten cottages, six restaurants, four retail outlets and a working farm, all on the Jersey Shore and Long Island's East End. Curtis lives in Cape May with his husband, Will.

☀️To all of Kamala Harris's supporters, Please do not click away. People are voting, and there are just days left until the final end-of-month fundraising deadline of this election. That means this is probably the most important time you could possibly make your first contribution to our campaign. If everyone reading this message donated even $10, we would not only have a huge number of contributions, but we wouldn't have to ask again before Election Day. But not everyone gives, so we're relying on people who understand how important keeping Donald Trump out of the White House is to chip in today. Our campaign is sustained by donations from only about 5% of Kamala's supporters. And without those gifts, big or small, we couldn't run a winning campaign. That's why we need your help. We are proud of our fundraising model, because at its core, this campaign is powered by people. Our average online contribution is around $60. Many donors give less. Some give more. body:
To stay ahead of Kari Lake, Donald Trump, and the outside groups backing them up in Arizona, we’re spending hundreds of thousands of dollars every day.
#

**Here’s where things stand with less than one week until our final monthly deadline of the election, Peter:**
To stay ahead of Kari Lake, Donald Trump, and the outside groups backing them up in Arizona, we’re spending hundreds of thousands of dollars every day. We’ve got to spend so heavily because we’re working to reach as many undecided voters as we possibly can. The primary way we do that is through advertising — online, on television, and on radio, too.
But at this point, we’ve almost completely spent down our reserves.
**What that means is just about every dollar we’ve ever raised has already been invested.**
That’s bad news, because Kari Lake is outspending Ruben on television in one of the most important parts of Arizona. She’s got more resources to burn through in these final weeks than we do. The timing, honestly, is terrible.
We’ve got to continue ramping up every day. If we don’t, we won’t reach the voters we need to turn out. We’ll cede ground to Lake and Trump. And that could cost us a seat in the U.S. Senate that we simply cannot afford to lose.
We can’t fall short now, and we wish we didn’t have to ask. [**But if you can afford it, will you help us keep up our momentum and make your first donation to Ruben’s campaign? | | | | | Dear ,
Our campaign for State House began over 10 months ago, and now Election Day is just 10 days away. I cannot thank everyone enough for their hard work and dedication—it’s because of you we will win on November 5th.
I know your time is valuable and your schedules are packed, but if you dedicate the next ten days to helping us get across the finish line, I will be able to fight for you every day as your next State Representative.
**BE A POLL WORKER**
We have 26 different polling locations that are each open 13 hours (7AM-8PM).Would you be able to help pass out information for our campaign for a few hours? If so, please just respond to this email, and we can work with you on a time and place.
**VOTE THIS WEEKEND**
This weekend, early voting will take place at the North Park Ice Rink from 9 AM to 5 PM on both Saturday (10/26) and Sunday (10/27). Any Allegheny County resident can vote in person or return their mail-in ballot during these hours.

We had a great time at the Trunk or Treat in Richland Park—I met and spoke with hundreds of other District 28 families. It was good seeing my friend Rob Mercuri and so many others who are energized and ready to win on November 5th!

The only people who can afford to run for Senate full-time are millionaires like my opponent, Republican Deb Fischer. That’s why they’re the only people who ever win. body:

[https://026s4.mjt.lu/img2/026s4/576d713f-627c-4b2a-9e49-73fa5c44b898/content]

We're drawing a line in the sand.
Electing more Democrats in Oregon will only make our situation worse. The gaslighting, false narratives, government overreach and power grabs must come to an end. 2022 is the year we draw the line in the sand.

As the House Republican Leader in Oregon, I have seen first hand the communist agenda of Kate Brown, Joe Biden and Ron Wyden - it is earth shattering to see their desire to ruin our country and our state. They want Republicans gone from Oregon.

The consequences of Democrats in the Oregon Legislature and Governor Brown have proven to be devastating for our families and our small businesses for years, now they are taking aim at our children.

DON’T LET THEM WIN. We can make a difference, but it needs to be this year. It needs to start today.

You have witnessed the hypocrisy, the political “science”, and utter destruction of kids in the school system. You see the truth. You see past the teachers union bosses and the power grabbing state agencies in Oregon.

In 2022, we get an opportunity to change the leadership in Oregon.

You have the opportunity to send a message to Kate Brown and liberal democrats that they have done enough damage to our state and our children’s future with their never-ending attack on small business, enabling government overreach and mandating school shutdowns. Enough is enough!
<<HELP STOP THE DEMOCRATS!>> [https://secure.winred.com/friends-of-vikki]

As the House Republican Leader, I am putting everything I have on the line. Will you help me win? Your contribution of $100, $250, $500, or $1000 is going to send a message - Enough.

Enough of Portland Democrats and liberal national agendas controlling our state. Portland Democrats can’t even control their own city from the nightly shootouts and rampant crime. They would rather put more criminals on the street, over hiring police to protect the citizens they were elected to serve.

National groups like the Republican State Leadership Committee are looking to turn the tide where it matters most—and Oregon is on their top-target list for the 2022 election.

We can WIN! But we need to raise $72,000 this month to reach critical deadlines.

Our team is ready to take majority in the Legislature and show that common-sense still has a place in our governing process. We are excited about our candidate recruitment effort this year; there is a path to victory. We have a campaign operation ready to win, but I need your help to do it.

Will you support me in making the strong effort to win in 2022? The RED WAVE is real, but we need to feed it, and push it to victory. We are going to every corner of the state–to every person who cares about the future of Oregon. Will you help? Will you be the difference in 2022 and bring balance to Oregon? We can win, but I need you today.

If you can make a contribution of $50, $250, $500, or even $1,000 to our fight, it will help us greatly in building a campaign effort that sends a message to Kate Brown, Joe Biden and socialist Democrat legislators–Not this year. Not Oregon.

For the future of Oregon.

Sincerely,

<<Vikki Breese Iverson Signature>> [https://026s4.mjt.lu/tplimg/026s4/b/1qm75/s4t3.png]

Vikki Breese-Iverson
House Republicans
Oregon State Representative for HD 59

P.S. Help us stop the over-taxing, over-spending, over-regulating and over-mandating of our lives. When we take back the Legislature, we will move quickly to advance an agenda to roll back mandates and taxes while putting our police back to work cleaning up our streets.

Fellow Conservative,

Yesterday was not a good fundraising day, and that is putting it lightly._** If I’m being totally honest, it was the worst day of the month so far.**_ Just 22 people donated to the email that I sent out yesterday, for a total of $370. If you read the note yesterday morning, you may recall that that email needed to raise $10,038—more than 27 times what we raised by the day’s end.
**
[If you’re able to contribute right now, please do.](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=41d2984db8e84d59b7c2eb708836f309&_e=RFeq5FvCji21zYI6XbJGkbHjThOCaoDi5mKz0W-kQ8E4UT2QujsfLCxLxcmqSlPCdTz-2fTjiYmMsvt74OpTZrH3xBsR1IHiIbwxDe5-mz011V92UHJqmFvCzfuUZSimu5NcShHNSHgy3htp0-d_OZvN8Dh6yj998eyfPqnzbwOOI2Aq80J1pyxahvcEqB3nkHQYyXGHc_390aGgqLvyctM1QqR0KZl2-8vkt4pydnDlVKG8lhX0mLVDSu4ApIlcWGOsULwVi09qY4EKWEclSr7KqMg9-h0unPHCxscn8-Ykbsy2KRGlaQ0B8zsG9cSzi6l5mIbf7f08t0nqT7Uk6DSKGv5qmQ7tw3WezjSfZJK8-jhGPzGePZyePswg3gbFLIcmiC14aU9SzTgbanbrNGyL6viRUY-L2pR7m2ilHMU%3D)** We have won nothing yet. We simply cannot let up until the final vote has been cast.
[**DONATE NOW ->** ](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=41d2984db8e84d59b7c2eb708836f309&_e=RFeq5FvCji21zYI6XbJGkbHjThOCaoDi5mKz0W-kQ8E4UT2QujsfLCxLxcmqSlPCdTz-2fTjiYmMsvt74OpTZrH3xBsR1IHiIbwxDe5-mz011V92UHJqmFvCzfuUZSimu5NcShHNSHgy3htp0-d_OZvN8Dh6yj998eyfPqnzbwOOI2Aq80J1pyxahvcEqB3nkHQYyXGHc_390aGgqLvyctM1QqR0KZl2-8vkt4pydnDlVKG8lhX0mLVDSu4ApIlcvO3NFcQEmQR3cyO1yOLtdsl5DtccUrKg3h3Y8BYgIRZuFkJVKMuNzNi5oJOLOVb9y7ku1TIKLzTLSlCJwIN5Pvv_QrHIyzIXGb38vtoWHRXcuiJSlZuBG8VaJUd2mYH0N5Nw7-nK0N9v0kB1Z6dvzMP6HzKaEEvfejk0t_O9HQw%3D)

I don’t want to sound like an alarmist, but yesterday’s fundraising totals shocked me. We’re 10 days from Election Day and must meet real fundraising goals to keep our campaign fully funded through November 5th. If we have another day like yesterday, tomorrow, or any remaining day in this campaign, flipping this seat will probably not happen.

body:
Derek –
We made a very difficult decision last week.
We had a Team Slotkin meeting where it became clear that if we had a bit more money, we could make a real play for additional votes as voting was underway across the state.
The money wasn’t in the budget. But I gave the green light.
It’s a risk. But this is the moment to take some risks. I’ve had similar moments in prior years. We can’t get caught short when people are already casting their ballots in this election. That'd be a mistake.
But the bet we made was that, as the race tightens, and if we asked, our supporters would come through to help fill the gap. We hope that you will. To keep the Senate in the hands of the Democrats.
So with that in mind: **[can you make a $10 contribution to John Fetterman and my campaign to help us fill the budget gap we created going after the voters we need to persuade to help win this race?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20241026?refcode=em20241026-9521&refcode2=9521_434096_RIYjM3&akid=9521%2E434096%2ERIYjM3)** $10 isn’t much, but at this point it’s the small-dollar donations that are making a difference here at the end.
Like I said, it was a tough call. But if there’s one thing that distinguishes this campaign from every other, it’s our people. body:
Back when Gabby first founded GIFFORDS in 2013, most politicians were too afraid to talk about gun violence. It was considered too politically divisive. But today, candidates run on gun violence prevention platforms—and they win.
#

During the 2022 elections, GIFFORDS PAC endorsed 288 candidates in races across the country, and 84% of these candidates won their elections.
That’s a big deal, and we’ll tell you why:
Back when Gabby first founded GIFFORDS in 2013, most politicians were too afraid to talk about gun violence. It was considered too politically divisive. But today, candidates run on gun violence prevention platforms—and they win. The progress we’ve been able to make in our movement for gun safety since 2013 is beyond Gabby’s wildest dreams.
This cycle, we’ve endorsed 342 gun safety candidates up and down the ballot, including Vice President Kamala Harris at the top of the ticket. We have the opportunity to make sure the vast majority of our endorsed candidates win this year like they did in 2022.
But to make that happen, we need your help in these last 10 days before Election Day to convince undecided voters to cast their ballots for leaders who will move us towards a future free from gun violence.

subject: VP Harris Joining Sunday Interfaith Call
body:
New Time: 6-7 pm ET Sun. Oct. 27 | |
---
| | | __**For all faith leaders, clergy, and organizers**__ - **please** **join Vice President Harris for a conversation and call to action** **TOMORROW – SUNDAY OCTOBER 27 from 6-7 pm ET. Note this is a new time from the notification that went out yesterday.**

**Please register [here](https://themaidengroup.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=417baae6ed2ee4b374c9c9805&id=32b7c8af6c&e=43463f1dee).**

All clergy, faith leaders, and organizers are invited to a **conversation with Vice President Harris** on the Faith for Harris-Walz [**Souls to the Polls Strategy call this Sunday October 27 from 6-7 pm ET**](https://themaidengroup.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=417baae6ed2ee4b374c9c9805&id=5004b3bfd0&e=43463f1dee).

**Please [invite your community](https://themaidengroup.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=417baae6ed2ee4b374c9c9805&id=e4b0076306&e=43463f1dee) to join this conversation between the Vice President and people of faith. **Share this [flyer](https://themaidengroup.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=417baae6ed2ee4b374c9c9805&id=6cd91af107&e=43463f1dee) with others.

**[Vice President Harris spoke to her faith](https://themaidengroup.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=417baae6ed2ee4b374c9c9805&id=164bc249d3&e=43463f1dee)** this week on CNN’s Town Hall with Anderson Cooper. She spoke of how prayer gets her through her day, and that faith is about action for justice in our world. The Vice President and campaign surrogates are visiting over a hundred houses of worship this weekend to get her message out as we move through early vote.

Please join Vice President Harris and other faith leaders on Sunday October 27 from 6-7 pm ET to bring the Harris-Walz message to your congregations and communities. You can also **share this **[**powerful video message from Vice President Harris**](https://themaidengroup.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=417baae6ed2ee4b374c9c9805&id=f9f22afe0b&e=43463f1dee)** during services, prayer breakfasts, social gatherings, broadcasts, and on social media.**

Thank you for all you’re doing. We’re praying for you.

Blessings,
The Evangelicals for Harris Team

Team,

**New data shows that in 2023 – the first full year where abortion rights were not protected by _Roe v. Wade_ – over 170,000 people were forced to travel across state lines to obtain abortion services, _double_ the number from 2020.**

The reason is clear: Right now in America, abortion access is either banned or severely curtailed in nearly half of states. In the south in particular, women have to travel hundreds of miles to reach a state where they can obtain care.

It isn’t just patients who are forced to travel, either. Every month, I drive several hours to Minnesota to practice medicine and treat patients – a drive I took up while abortion was banned here in Wisconsin.

**No one should have to leave home in order to get the care they need, or worse, to go without it entirely.** But that’s what’s happening under Trump’s abortion bans.

**[_We need to put an end to this. In Congress, I’ll work to codify protection for reproductive health care. Please, pitch in to my campaign right now._](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/95870440/508153642/1319362643?refcode=KL_ATA_EM_FR_OutofState_241026_T1_1&utm_source=kl_ata_em_fr_outofstate_241026_t1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NDIyNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2Y2ZjZDlmNS1hYTkzLWVmMTEtODhjZS0wMDBkM2E5OGZhNmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=htcSPiJqvZPMryTmKYd2VeBHNGyLSvdQIlQeFlCXP10=)**

If Donald Trump wins again – and gets a rubber stamp in Congress, which my opponent has promised to be – _it’ll get worse._

Project 2025 would create a national abortion database to track pregnant women, overrule medical experts at the FDA and reverse approval of the abortion pill, and even attack contraception access. It’s a nightmare for public health, and for women.

**[_We can stop it – but we need to win. Please, chip in to my campaign for Congress right now >>_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/95870443/508153650/1319362643?refcode=KL_ATA_EM_FR_OutofState_241026_T1_1&utm_source=kl_ata_em_fr_outofstate_241026_t1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NDIyNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2Y2ZjZDlmNS1hYTkzLWVmMTEtODhjZS0wMDBkM2E5OGZhNmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=htcSPiJqvZPMryTmKYd2VeBHNGyLSvdQIlQeFlCXP10=)**

Thank you,

Kristin Lyerly

Derek,
Sherrod Brown and Jon Tester are running for re-election in two red states — Ohio and Montana — that could determine control of the Senate. So many critical issues are at stake, from reproductive freedom to eliminating corruption in our government.
With just 10 days until Election Day, every single dollar will help these campaigns reach the voters who could decide their races. That’s why we’re emailing you today.
**[Will you rush a contribution to Sherrod Brown, Jon Tester, and Truth to Power to help Democrats hold onto our slim Senate majority?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ttp-em-20241026-1?refcode=em20241026-39225&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=39225_3422442_lzf7P3&akid=39225%2E3422442%2Elzf7P3)**

Team Truth to Power

Leaders We Deserve is counting on your support before October 31.

Peter, this is a pretty big moment for Leaders We Deserve.
We’re on the cusp of electing a slate of 13 young progressive candidates to Congress and competitive state legislative seats – and we’re facing our last big deadline before Election Day.
**[I’m personally setting a goal for this grassroots team to raise $75,000 before October 31. Can we count on your support to fuel the next generation of bold leaders to victory? Make a contribution of $5 or anything you can now.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20241026?refcode=em20241026-1363&amount=5&refcode2=1363_587540_D1cAFk&akid=1363%2E587540%2ED1cAFk)**

From knocking on doors for our candidates in Texas to broadcasting our vision on The Daily Show, I’ve had a busy few weeks. With the election so close – and some of these races likely decided by just a handful of votes – we need to leave it all on the field. **We don’t want to wake up on November 6th wishing we had done more.**

And earlier this year, we helped Molly Cook win a special election AND a primary in Texas, making her the youngest and first LGBTQ+ state senator in Texas history.
After November 5th, that list can be much longer. We can elect a whole slate of young progressive candidates who will fight for the issues that matter most.

**Curtis Bashaw is a hotel entrepreneur, job creator, and preservationist. He's running for United States Senate to provide greater freedom and opportunities for all New Jerseyans.**

A lifelong New Jersey resident, Curtis grew up in Camden County and spent his summers at the Jersey Shore working as a bellhop and waiting tables at Congress Hall in Cape May. Throughout his career, Curtis has worked to build communities and bring people together. Curtis' company owns and operates eight hotels, ten cottages, six restaurants, four retail outlets and a working farm, all on the Jersey Shore and Long Island's East End. Curtis lives in Cape May with his husband, Will.

# When We Vote We Win!

_Dear Friends,_
_I want to take a moment to express my heartfelt gratitude to everyone who participated in the Canvass and Rally hosted by myself, Dr. Prabhu Rachakonda, and Reuben D'Silva. Your presence and support mean the world to us!_
_This is where grassroots support truly makes a difference. Your contributions help fund our efforts to mobilize thousands of volunteers and staff who are actively knocking on doors, making phone calls, and engaging with voters. It’s essential that we communicate Kamala's record of progress and problem-solving, and help people understand the real threat posed by another four years of Trump’s chaos._
_I know I’ve reached out many times before, but with less than two weeks until the elections and millions of voters in swing states already casting their ballots, I urge you to chip in today—whatever you can give will make a significant impact.__For those who couldn’t join us, I’ve included a video below capturing highlights from our massive volunteer canvassing event in Las Vegas last weekend._
_Thank you once again for your unwavering support. Together, we can ensure a brighter future for our country!_
_Best,_
_Dr. Asif Mahmood_

name: Elissa Slotkin
subject: Elon Musk’s cynical ploy in MI
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELISSA SLOTKIN FOR MICHIGAN
body:
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2122%2E135344%2EtPhBog)

Friend,
In the six years since I entered the political world, I have seen a lot of lies and cynical tactics. A lot. But the play being run by PACs tied to right-wing billionaire Elon Musk is a new low.
A PAC largely funded by Elon Musk called “Future Coalition PAC” is sending mailers and texts, and targeting digital ads to the Jewish, Arab, and Muslim communities in Michigan and Pennsylvania with opposite messages.
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-oct24.UCjdR-&refcode=em241026-2-900&t=2&akid=2122%2E135344%2EtPhBog)
To Jewish voters, they accuse Vice President Kamala Harris of “emboldening anti-semites” and being insufficiently supportive of Israel.
To Arab and Muslim voters, they claim Harris has given “unwavering support for Israel.” Even more cynically, they feature photos of Harris and her Jewish husband, Doug Emhoff, calling them the “ultimate pro-Israel power couple” and saying that the Vice President “leans on Jewish husband Doug Emhoff to advise on high level pro-Israel policies.”

Please see a special message from our sponsor:

Dear
Fellow American,

I am
enclosing a survey on a very urgent matter.

It will
only take a moment of your time, but the topic is vital to our
nation's future.

A
movement is growing, led by progressives-but supported by many
well-meaning Americans-to change the way we elect our president.
In effect, it seeks to do away with the Electoral College as
devised by the Framers of our Constitution.

That's
why Hillsdale College is conducting a National Survey on
Presidential Selection.

By
completing this survey and returning it to me as soon as
possible, you will help Hillsdale College more clearly understand
the views of mainstream Americans concerning this issue-views we
will make available to policymakers and opinion leaders.

You can
complete the National Survey on Presidential Selection by using
the link below:
http://paracom.paramountcommunication.com/ct/63668059:WZkXFMWN4:m:3:2532013465:C578957E757EE376DD8869D3E9AA0D5B:r

Do you
think that most Americans understand how the Electoral College
works and its role in preserving free and representative
government?
YES
NO

For most
of our nation's history, the Electoral College, as devised by the
Framers of our Constitution, was not controversial. Indeed, it
was considered essential to preserving free and representative
government.

But
today, more than a dozen states have joined together in an
attempt to undermine this constitutional bulwark of liberty.

This
movement to undermine the Constitution has grown largely because
of the failure of America's schools to provide young people with
a proper grounding in American civics-too many Americans simply
don't understand the importance of the Constitution, including
the Electoral College, to liberty.

Because
of this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission
on behalf of liberty nationwide, directly teaching millions of
Americans in all 50 states.

These
efforts, which aim to counter the Left's domination over most of
our schools, include:

Teaching millions of citizens nationwide through free online
courses, such as "Constitution 101" and "The Great American
Story: A Land of Hope;"

Reaching over six million households and businesses nationwide
with Imprimis, Hillsdale's free digest of liberty;

Promoting constitutional education through social media outlets
popular with young people;

Sending millions of pocket-size copies of America's founding
documents to citizens and K-12 schools across America; and

Restoring excellence to K-12 education by helping establish and
guiding classical K-12 schools nationwide and providing, free of
charge, Hillsdale's American classical K-12 curriculum (including
American civics) to thousands of American educators and
homeschoolers.

Your
answers to the National Survey on Presidential Selection will
help Hillsdale form the most effective strategy to educate
millions of Americans about the importance of the Constitution to
liberty-including the importance of the Electoral College.

And this
is especially important in this critical time for America's
future.

So please
share your views on this urgent topic by completing our National
Survey on Presidential Selection and returning it to me as soon
as possible. It will only take a few minutes of your time.

You can
take the survey using this secure link I've provided below:
http://paracom.paramountcommunication.com/ct/63668059:WZkXFMWN4:m:3:2532013465:C578957E757EE376DD8869D3E9AA0D5B:r

And after
you take your survey, I hope you will also consider supporting
Hillsdale College with a tax-deductible gift.

Since
1844, Hillsdale has been "pursuing truth and defending liberty."
Today, it does so through its extensive educational outreach
efforts while refusing to accept ONE PENNY of government
funding-not even indirectly in the form of federal or state
student grants or loans.

The
support of private citizens like you is essential to our work.

Please
represent your state and take the National Survey on Presidential
Selection today. Thank you for your time and attention-and for
your friendship and support of liberty.

Warm
regards,

Larry P.
Arnn

President, Hillsdale College
Pursuing
Truth and Defending Liberty Since 1844

Can I explain something, folks?
I grew up in a 24-by-36 foot house. I lost three fingers on my left hand in a meat grinding accident when I was a kid. I am and always will be a farmer, like my folks and my grandparents before me.

**In fact, I’m very proud to be the U.S. Senate’s only working dirt farmer.**
Every spring, I spend a lot of weeks working the stubble, getting equipment ready for planting, and out in the field seeding. Come summer, I am out there harvesting. I maintain my own heavy equipment and deliver my grain in a truck that’s a bit bigger than what any of my colleagues drive.

I buy grease by the case and seeds by the ton. I butcher my own beef. My wife, Sharla, and I work the farm hand-in-hand.
The task of scheduling my work in the Senate around the inflexible timing of farm responsibilities drives my staff crazy — but they know my farm work is non-negotiable. It keeps me, quite literally, grounded.

**And rather than spend my days hobnobbing with special interests, I rely on hardworking folks like you to power everything we do.**
**[That’s why I’m personally asking you to join my reelection team and split $5 between Jeanne Shaheen and my campaign today to help us defend Montana’s Senate seat. Anything you can give makes a difference.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/95877871/508178086/175992266?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&amount=5&refcode=jtk3018-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDQvMS84ODk1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhM2Q0NGQxMC1iNDkzLWVmMTEtODhjZS0wMDBkM2E5OGZhNmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LZQ4L5sS8QAnlxJ4X_Yk9oM4-k7An2JrEVHoMkaPXkU=)** | | [Contribute](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/95877872/508178087/175992266?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk3018-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDQvMS84ODk1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhM2Q0NGQxMC1iNDkzLWVmMTEtODhjZS0wMDBkM2E5OGZhNmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LZQ4L5sS8QAnlxJ4X_Yk9oM4-k7An2JrEVHoMkaPXkU=)

Peter,
On Friday, _The Washington Post_ announced that, for the first time in 40 years, it would not endorse a candidate in the 2024 presidential election.
The outlet—whose slogan is “Democracy dies in darkness”—claimed an editorial shift as the reason for this decision, even as Donald Trump openly runs as a fascist, and polls show a historically close race.
[**We’ll unpack this more in a moment, but if you support COURIER’s efforts to call out legacy media for failing to defend democracy, can you chip in $25 now?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/95878980/508182123/-260044646?refcode=20241026-EM-WaPoEndorsement&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMTc1NTFjNTItYjQ5My1lZjExLTg4Y2UtMDAwZDNhOThmYTZiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=5mcfeY_UNZTRz_06piv13Ho8JWmRZ1-HANiLvXnVS4M=)

Yet, in this climate, _The Washington Post_ has chosen to stay silent. It’s pure cowardice, happening even as their own journalists face increasing threats of violence from Trump’s relentless demonization of the press.
36% of journalists now report harassment or violence on the job, especially at Trump rallies where hostility toward the press is encouraged.
**As Americans head to the polls, what message does it send that one of the nation’s most respected newspapers won’t stand against the creeping fascism threatening a free press?**
While _The Washington Post_ capitulates to Trump, COURIER remains resolute: our democracy cannot afford a fascist in the White House.

| | Dear Friend,

Citizens are free to say what they think. Subjects aren't.

Sadly, the question of whether we are citizens or subjects has become politically controversial in our country. A clear sign of this is the attempt to suppress the expression of obvious truths, such as the fact that boys cannot become girls.

Another sign that many of our leaders consider us subjects is their denial of our right to decide who is allowed to enter our country--indeed, they tell us that if we complain about mass illegal immigration, we are racists.

**This is a pivotal time in our nation 's history--a time when we must stand up and forthrightly demand to be treated as citizens, not subjects. Because freedom hangs in the balance.**

A poisonous ideology has infected almost every major American institution. Only a few still stand in defense of freedom and the right of self-government.

One of the most important of these is **Hillsdale College**. And today, my friends at Hillsdale need your partnership and support in their mission to preserve the blessings of civil and religious liberty through education.

For 180 years, Hillsdale has offered its students the kind of education America's founders thought necessary to sustain free government. And in recent decades, Hillsdale has extended its teaching mission nationwide with a vast national outreach effort.

This outreach effort includes its free publication _Imprimis_ , its free online courses, and its tireless work to return excellence--including excellent civics instruction--to American K-12 education.

And Hillsdale College does all of this while refusing to accept one penny of government funding--not even indirectly through federal or state student grants and loans.

There has been a nationwide shortage of the essential IV fluids that are necessary to perform surgery, save lives during an emergency, keep patients alive in hospitals, mix medications, irrigate and clean wounds, perform dialysis and many other medical treatments.
**Saline is essential for almost every medical procedure and critical to the survival of our sickest.**
Thanks for reading Michael's Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..n2-uPp4piwMRL_QgF-nfM9DoW2hQ0AJTGYd3cdzhXbw?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=150763405)
This administration should have learned from the COVID Pandemic that supply chain shortages of essential medications and equipment cost lives. We should have learned from hurricanes in Puerto Rico that disrupted our healthcare supply chain.
Ensuring that we have a robust supply chain in healthcare should have been a priority but it wasn't.
Along comes a hurricane and one factory that manufactures 60% of the saline solutions shuts down probably _**until early next year**_. **Diversification is critical in any industry.**
This should be the simplest problem to solve. We are talking about sterile diluted salt water. The only solution right now is to react using the Defense Production Act but in the meantime we are just importing Saline with the first airlift on October 19th but that is not a pro-active.
_**Except for the sterile part and the packaging you could make this in your kitchen.**_
We have created too many regulatory hurdles to make the manufacturing of what should be a simple product like dilute salt water is not profitable enough to produce it in sufficient quantities in this country to meet our needs.
**We also do not have a streamlined process for another company to step in and manufacture the saline.**
Most legislators are unaware of the complexities of our healthcare system and how what should be simple problems with simple solutions can paralyze our healthcare system.
**It is time to Put a Doctor In The House to for the Healthcare Fix we need.**
Make America Healthy Again and vote for Michael Goldstein for Congress Row 3B.

By [Berkeley Lovelace Jr.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/2190ff74-b8c6-4b3b-aa2f-4f072930c0b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Years before Hurricane Helene [shut down a critical intravenous fluid facility in North Carolina](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a2f6e11e-2f99-4be6-bf74-4eb31f57f389?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), sparking concerns in hospitals across the country, many common IV fluids were already in short supply in the U.S.
Saline solution, a mixture of sodium chloride and water, has been in shortage since 2018, [according to the Food and Drug Administration's drug shortage database](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/50255d19-4fc3-46b9-b6f5-fa65152f8e07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Saline drips, which provide hydration, are a frequent sight in hospitals. And sterile water, which is used to mix with medications, dilute other fluids or clean wounds, has been in [shortage since 2021](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/be9427e9-1182-41a1-b82a-85ce1dfbe9fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
And several concentrations of dextrose, a sugar solution used to help patients who can't eat, have low blood sugar or need extra energy, have been in short supply [since early 2022](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/61f89b9a-5a23-4fe9-91c8-e3b1e4e9977e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Helene's damage to the Baxter International plant in North Carolina triggered several additional shortages, [the FDA said last week](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4d98ceb1-9e6e-4c70-9aef-b0b82c5d4d6e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), including another concentration of dextrose solution, along with an electrolyte solution called lactated Ringer's and a peritoneal dialysis solution for patients with kidney failure.
So, why are these essential fluids -- [a lifeline for hospitals](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/627d5021-33fd-4df4-b291-a37f93c38a35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- so hard to come by?
As is often the case with drug shortages, it comes down to money, and IV fluids don't bring in much of it for manufacturers, said Erin Fox, senior pharmacy director at the University of Utah Health.
"These are life-saving products, but at the same time these are absolutely treated as kind of commodities," Fox said.
The high barrier to entry -- including the time and cost required to meet the regulatory requirements for setting up a manufacturing facility -- along with the pressure to keep prices low, means drugmakers aren't really motivated to jump into the market, Fox said.
IV fluids, she said, also require an extraordinary amount of space: A single bag of saline, for example, is about the size of a loaf of bread and weighs just over 2 pounds.
"So not just any space, but also has to be able to hold heavy weight," Fox said.
To complicate matters, these products are difficult to make -- even sterile water or saline solution.
"I know everyone is like, 'It's just salt and water! What do you mean?'" Fox said. "But making sure that everything is completely sterile and particle-free and really safe to give inside someone's vein is a lot of work."
Michael Ganio, senior director of pharmacy practice and quality at the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists, a group that tracks drug shortages in the U.S., said that a significant concern is endotoxins, harmful substances found in bacteria that can cause a strong immune reaction in the body, including fever and inflammation. Endotoxins are highly resistant to sterilization, meaning manufacturers have to continuously monitor and control for their presence.
"There are multiple tests that go into these generic injectables, and yet, the prices don't reflect a lot of that additional work that has to go into it," Ganio said.
In the U.S., the IV fluid market is sustained primarily by four manufacturers: Baxter International, which makes about 60% of the country's IV liquids; B. Braun Medical, which makes about 23%; followed by ICU Medical and Fresenius Kabi.
That means when one manufacturer shuts down, it hits U.S. hospitals hard, Fox said.
"Any little glitch in the system can really disrupt things and create some shortages," said Fox, who said her hospital hasn't received any IV fluid shipments since the end of September. "Unless we're going to pay these companies to have extra capacity that is sitting there waiting -- which is very, very expensive -- this is a shortage that we can't stockpile our way out of."
**Government invokes wartime power**
Hospitals have grown accustomed to situations like the Baxter facility shutting down, said Dr. Chris DeRienzo, a neonatologist and the chief physician executive of the American Hospital Association. In 2017, Hurricane Maria damaged three IV fluid manufacturing plants in Puerto Rico, also operated by Baxter, which led to a shortage.
"Although this particular shortage on these particular IV fluids is not something we've encountered," DeRienzo said. Along with IV fluids, the North Carolina Baxter facility also made specialty fluids, such as peritoneal dialysis fluid as well as irrigation fluids, used to clean wounds.
In the case of the Baxter closure, the federal government has been racing to fill the gap. The Department of Health and Human Services announced last week that it invoked the Defense Production Act, a wartime power that will help Baxter obtain materials to clean and rebuild its facility. Under the law, Baxter will get priority access to certain materials, even if there are shortages or supply disruptions, and access to funding to scale up production.
The FDA is also temporarily allowing Baxter to import products from its plants in Canada, China, Ireland and the U.K.
On Tuesday, a spokesperson for HHS said the efforts had led to a 50% increase in available IV fluid products compared to shortly after the Baxter plant closed. Hospitals had been reporting getting only 40% of their usual shipments from the company.
Ganio said those measures won't solve the ongoing IV fluid shortage problems long term.
That may require incentives, such as a guarantee that over time companies will make a profit on their products. This is a critical issue for the entire generic drug market, he said, including for other drugs in shortages like cancer treatments.
"The IV fluids are kind of a good example of the chronic shortages," he said.

Friend.

Chuck Schumer and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee are now jumping into this race to rescue endangered career politician Martin Heinrich.

**They’re funneling out-of-state dollars into New Mexico to buy up precious advertising time during the final weeks and days before Election Day.**

They know they were completely caught off guard when I entered this race and have been watching nervously as we’ve gradually caught up to Heinrich in the polls.

Now, they can’t stand to sit by any longer and are frantically trying to stop our upward momentum.

With New Mexico being one of the smallest states and cheapest media markets in the 2024 fight for the Senate, the money they’ve raised from West and East Coast liberal elites stretches much further here, _which means they can do A LOT more damage with much less._

But that also means your support goes much further here, [**and I’m asking you to help rebalance the scales and prevent Schumer and his deep-pocketed allies from buying this election at the last minute.**](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=8d585f45fa5c4d79af32137fb74a9ca6&_e=Lw4-Q61CQDaPEzKsz98RGCP4EZ1295Rew3wnnfeaeWzI8k-d-L1gUy69UV4T4Vs2QMiRZL5J9aS9x_DOHUR39HpJtDXSF53KBIVTaxr2ugT8CFfiklVlYnK56IotdTV4gnMPQd_A1Yq7fgoVQ2WNdYrUPpL03GyVJzVdl8t0GfkAI-OyGd9zCdv-gS9XcxjXdXP1hgNlB03415evmInCCIz7yjQ82BOBtVj5-ehe4tHnZFF2YtTDUoOpRR4hbDLLwb3Ap_N8Q4a4dpt5CKGd3MXeQBwUdyfA6lMnulCf-NYCYlG02dvc5GubNf4Ycn3FNUc3jgl7y3-x_fGA7ELP_87E8jVD5EtSPtmR8W83exysv_hGXanZnd-AARrjcK1jmjuEzsGa2TiZHqmfDbpjeA%3D%3D)

We’ve never been so close to flipping a “safe blue” state, and I need every bit of support you can send down the home stretch.

[**Whether it’s $5 or $500, every dollar donated at this point in the campaign helps us reach and win over undecided voters in this race.**](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=8d585f45fa5c4d79af32137fb74a9ca6&_e=Lw4-Q61CQDaPEzKsz98RGCP4EZ1295Rew3wnnfeaeWzI8k-d-L1gUy69UV4T4Vs2QMiRZL5J9aS9x_DOHUR39HpJtDXSF53KBIVTaxr2ugT8CFfiklVlYnK56IotdTV4gnMPQd_A1Yq7fgoVQ2WNdYrUPpL03GyVJzVdl8t0GfkAI-OyGd9zCdv-gS9XcxjXdXP1hgNlB03415evmInCCIz7yjQ82BOBtVj5-ehe4tHnZFF2YtTDUoOpRR4hbDLLHNoF_xHaPEeqY4uZe54PGGPuGa7bWXzWtKW_Ot44iq_E57CbNizYIZv4pj_0YYm8fjbug-LSUEKIZVSAdtYOZeLkeP2hEimHu6qQN9R1ST4EwV8EpIrxS2U7Sc-8dmkrK2iHvs5iWMeXdLpomXJhTQ%3D%3D)

**Nella Domenici**
Republican for Senate

| **ABOUT NELLA**
**New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years.

Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant.

Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. Collectively, the companies Nella has been heavily involved with have employed thousands of Americans.

Like her father and mother, Nella has been a warrior for those who most need an advocate: for women competing in academics or business, for families dealing with mental illness, and for those without access to quality healthcare or education. **

[ ** JOIN NELLA **](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=8d585f45fa5c4d79af32137fb74a9ca6&_e=Lw4-Q61CQDaPEzKsz98RGCP4EZ1295Rew3wnnfeaeWzI8k-d-L1gUy69UV4T4Vs2QMiRZL5J9aS9x_DOHUR39HpJtDXSF53KBIVTaxr2ugT8CFfiklVlYnK56IotdTV4gnMPQd_A1Yq7fgoVQ2WNdYrUPpL03GyVJzVdl8t0GfkAI-OyGd9zCdv-gS9XcxjXdXP1hgNlB03415evmInCCIz7yjQ82BOBtVj5-ehe4tHnZFF2YtTDUoOpRR4hbDLL8Yu16Q8y8ShCGCA79ct2U9YGwsiuXsu2gQ7SbN7WGOlkY4mEGaVbkHQ27pg5RLrqdwCJZfUOyUmIRP6E4LYyCr80cBlgMx-vQQvHKSfSz2tYPUzPyWrTg3uhXEY14wUcJU0kvKE9thnTu-_6l9zAvw%3D%3D)
